title: SDK request decorator and attribute stabilizer for cross-service telemetry
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a lightweight SDK-level request decorator that stabilizes a small set of trace attributes across retries, proxies, and language SDKs. Goal: reduce noisy attribute churn in traces (service, route_fingerprint, client_region, request_stage) so latency and error dashboards can reliably group and alert. The decorator should: (1) normalize and canonicalize common headers across edge proxies, (2) compute a stable request fingerprint when upstream ids are missing, (3) attach sampling hints and deterministic sampling keys for downstream routing, and (4) be opt-in with a backward-compatible header format. Target low overhead (<100ns avg allocation per request in Go SDK) and graceful degradation for legacy clients.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Go, Python, Node) expose request decorator API and default behavior enabled for Redwood-hosted customers
Stable attribute set appears on 99% of sampled spans for request volumes in staging; attribute churn reduced by >=75% on test traffic
End-to-end unit and integration tests covering header normalization, fingerprint generation, retry consistency, and sampling hint propagation
Benchmarks show <5% p50 latency regression and <10% p99 regression on SDK request path in microbenchmarks
Migration doc and console toggle for turning feature off per-customer without requiring SDK deployment
comments: 2025-01-27 — Asha: Created ticket after spike showing noisy trace attributes from edge rewrite. Proposed decorator approach to keep changes local to SDKs.

2025-01-30 — Marcello: Implemented PoC in Go SDK (branch: feature/sdk-decorator-stable-attrs). PoC computes fingerprint using prefix of request-id + client-cert-fingerprint fallback. Microbench shows ~80ns median allocation per request.
2025-02-03 — Design review: PM/Observability approved attribute list: service, route_fingerprint, client_region, trace_generation_epoch. Agreed to avoid PII. Linked Confluence spec (see attachments).

2025-02-06 — QA: Added integration tests simulating proxy header rewrites and double-retries. Noted edge case when upstream sets conflicting id headers — default to canonical header ordering per spec.
2025-02-10 — Eng: Opened PR for Go and Node SDK adapters: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/5543. Benchmarks attached; need Python follow-up.

steps: Finalize canonical header list and normalization rules in spec
Implement decorator API surface in Go SDK and provide default implementation
Port default implementation to Node and Python SDKs with language-specific low-overhead optimizations
Add deterministic fingerprint generator with stable seeding and collision analysis
Add sampling-hint propagation mechanism compatible with current tracing pipeline
Create integration tests simulating proxies, retries, and partial header loss
Run perf benchmarks across p50/p95/p99 and memory allocations; iterate if >10% regression
Prepare migration/rollout plan and console toggle; communicate to customers and solutions engineers
perf_regression_risks: Primary risk is allocation overhead in high-throughput SDK paths if fingerprint generation is not zero-allocation. Mitigations: use stack buffers, preallocated pools for Node/Python, and optional compile-time flags to disable fingerprinting. Also risk of increased trace volume if attribute set expands — acceptance criteria caps attribute list.
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization rules and header precedence
Property tests for fingerprint stability across retries and header loss
End-to-end integration tests with edge proxy simulator and Redwood ingest pipeline in staging
Performance regression tests using existing SDK bench harness against baseline
Canary rollout with 5% traffic for dedicated and hosted customers, monitor error/latency dashboards
